title: Mathan born
summary: A second son is born to the household of Clann a' Chlachair at Tobar dhìreach, three years before his brother Fearghas, a long-legged child who from the first is surer on wet rock than any of the kin his own age.

title: Fearghas born
summary: Fearghas is born at Tobar dhìreach into Clann a' Chlachair, growing up on Gormal's unsettled riddle of the three hills as every child of the line grows up on it, turning the six dark coals over in his own hands before he is old enough to feel either the wonder or the doubt older mouths bring to the same handling.

title: Mathan names the fault in Gormal's three hills
summary: Mathan says aloud, to his brother, what each of them has been turning over apart: that Gormal named her three hills from where she stood and never climbed higher than her own doorstep to judge between them, and that the line has legs enough to settle the question by walking rather than by arguing at the hearth.

title: The brothers stand on the first of Gormal's three hills
summary: Fearghas and Mathan climb the hill south of the black well, the nearest of the three heights Gormal once named, and standing on its crown cannot agree between them whether the shoulder of moor she had favoured stands higher still, learning only that no one of the three can be judged fairly against the others without climbing each in turn.

title: A herder of the southern moor points beyond the known ground
summary: An old herder driving his flock along a saddle of moor tells the two brothers of a further shoulder his own father swore stood higher than anything nearer the valleys, though the father himself never went to prove it, and sends them on with nothing but the names of a burn and a stand of thorn to steer by.

title: A climb lost to rain
summary: Fearghas and Mathan climb the shoulder the herder's father had sworn by and stand on it in a driving rain that shows them nothing of the ground beyond, coming down soaked and short-tempered with each other over whether the wetting had been worth it.

title: The true height is sighted
summary: In clearer weather three summers into their walking, Fearghas and Mathan come out from behind a shoulder of bare rock and see, standing above every other height in every direction, a grey summit with cloud dragging along its crown, and know without needing to say it that the walking is nearly done.

title: The brothers set out for the height
summary: Carrying the six dark coals wrapped against the wet in the leather bag, Fearghas and Mathan climb through the last night of summer toward the summit that stands clear over the whole island, sleeping little for the wind and going up with the first grey of morning.

title: Mathan sets the first stone of the cairn
summary: Before the brothers leave the summit where gual sneachda has just taken fire in the falling air, Mathan sets one loose stone from the crown atop another, a small cairn no higher than a hand, and says nothing over it that needs saying.

title: The telling reaches every hearth within a day's walk
summary: By the morning after Fearghas and Mathan tell it standing at Tobar dhìreach, with the four cold coals laid out on a cloth for any hand to turn over, word of the lighting on the height has gone out to every household within a day's walk, carried by whoever heard it first and could not keep from carrying it further.

title: The first stone left by a stranger's hand
summary: A herder of the high valleys, passing within sight of the grey summit for the first time since the telling went out, climbs to Mathan's small cairn and lays a stone of his own beside it, the first stone set there by a hand not of Clann a' Chlachair, beginning a custom that outlives everyone then living.

title: Fearghas climbs the height with his son
summary: Fearghas, his hair gone grey, climbs the height a second time with his own son grown old enough for the way, and shows him the white fire still burning steady among the cold stones below the summit exactly as he had first seen it catch, unchanged in every particular.

title: Mathan dies
summary: Mathan dies of a fever that comes on him in a wet spring and will not break, five and fifty years old, and is buried at Tobar dhìreach with the first cairn stone he ever set on the height closed in one hand at his own asking, having given the height, as he put it himself, three summers of his legs and his best notion.

title: Fearghas's last climb
summary: An old man now, three days each way instead of two, Fearghas climbs to the height a last time alone and finds the white coal burning exactly as he left it every time before, and leaves a stone of his own on the crown before coming down for good.

title: Fearghas dies
summary: Fearghas dies at Tobar dhìreach in his sixty-second year, sure to the last of his own two feet on the height he had proved, and is buried within sight of Leac na Fèithe that covers the mason's vein as every keeper and finder of the line is buried before him.

title: Fearghas's name is added to the recital
summary: At the recital said over Fearghas's grave, the reciter gives his name for the first time after his father's in the fixed words of the fathers of the line, telling how he climbed to the top of the island and let the six coals fall, and how the snowflake took fire in the empty air and gave the summit its name.
